hypothesis: Uncertainty over whether/how often the latent sparse relation changes can preserve stationary evidence without fixing the learner permanently in a no-change model.

observed_failure.interpretation: Fixed hazard worsened stationary error. This motivates uncertainty over hazard, not a posthoc claim that the fixed-rate design worked.

budget_decision_before_execution.decision: Nine-state compression is strongly harmful on recurrence. Use32 per hazard (128 live branches total) for v6; fixed32 children isolate hazard averaging within the same per-child approximation. Higher compute/state cost is explicit, not a budget-matched claim.

hyper_update: Past-only hazard weights produce current forecast; afterward multiply by each child's PRE-TRUNCATION Gaussian-mixture predictive density and normalize. No fixed share or hyperposterior forgetting.
selection: No test-based hyperparameter selection. Budget32 chosen from v5 development recurrence failure before v6 execution; hazard grid/hyperprior fixed beforehand. Original AdamW lock authenticated before draws. Hyperweights update only from online noisy observations. Namespace200 configurations fixed before any fresh outcomes.
metrics: full and postchange prequential clean/noisy MSE
final exact Bernoulli risk including stale-support partition
promotion: Fresh change error at least20% below v3-static, stationary regression <=5%, null absolute clean risk<=1e-5. Publish recurrent/two-support stresses and all children, not only the best arm.
limitations: Four fixed hazard hypotheses approximate an unknown process
Hyperposterior has a constant-hazard assumption and can accumulate selection debt
Four children cost more than one filter
Informative sparsity prior is not supplied to AdamW; no generic optimizer superiority claim
One seed with named fresh streams, no seed-level significance
Biological analogy is not supporting evidence
